props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · unshaded 3D quad · Forward+ above, Compatibility below · Apple M4 Pro
props.caption: Forward+: default on desktop · Compatibility: widest hardware, default on web

B27.capture_spec: C22: two Lab renders of lab-shaders/20-blend-3d.gdshader (quad3d, 1280x360 logical each), vstack: top --renderer forward_plus, bottom --renderer gl_compatibility; stills. Verified at the middle (0.5, 0.5): Forward+ 0.600, Mobile 0.600, Compatibility 0.502; at 0.1: 0.329 / 0.333 / 0.259; at 0.9: 0.765 / 0.765 / 0.741. GATE T note: the 0.2 gray end is dark; strips are tall, so they are not text-shaped.
B27.visual_intent: Act title 'Two Ways to Count Light' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left (a spatial unshaded shader that mixes two source-color grays by UV.x). At right two real horizontal gray strips stacked, the same shader in two renderers: top labelled 'Forward+', bottom 'Compatibility'. A readout at the middle of the top strip '0.60', then at the middle of the bottom strip '0.50'.
B27.motion_claim: The two strips differ visibly at the middle, and the readouts land top then bottom.
B27.why: The two strips side by side let the eye see the gap before the numbers say it; this is the film's central surprise.

B28.visual_intent: A left-to-right chain of four outline boxes: 'numbers you typed', 'shader math', 'the renderer', 'pixel on screen'. A terracotta token travels the chain. A magnifier (a circle and a handle) lands on the last box with the label 'probe: reads one pixel's color'. Under the chain a second, shorter chain 'no window' leads to a box 'no pixels' that is struck through, labelled 'null'.
B28.motion_claim: The token travels the chain and the magnifier lands at its end; the lower chain stops at an empty box.

show.event: magnifier on the last box: a probe reads here; settled through 60 %
second chain: no window, no pixels, null

B28.why: A pipeline with the probe at its very end shows that a probe sees only the last box's output; a table cannot show where the magnifier sits.

B29.visual_intent: Axes: the horizontal axis 'typed number (sRGB: the scale color pickers use)' from 0 to 1, the vertical 'light (linear: numbers that add up like light)' from 0 to 1. A dashed diagonal marked 'if the two agreed'. The real sRGB curve is drawn from (0, 0) to (1, 1), bending under the diagonal. Rings on the two ends where it meets the diagonal. A dot slides along the curve to x = 0.5 and drops a dashed line to y = 0.21 with the label '0.5 typed = 0.21 light'.
B29.motion_claim: The curve draws itself under the diagonal; a dot rides it and drops to 0.21 at 0.5.

show.event: the curve draws; rings on both ends
dot at x = 0.5 drops to 0.21; settled through 60 %
hold with the gap between curve and diagonal labelled

B29.why: A curve under a diagonal is exactly 'the two scales agree at the ends and disagree between'; a render could not show a scale.

B30.visual_intent: The same axes and curve. Two dots on the curve at typed 0.2 and 0.8 (light 0.03 and 0.60) joined by a thin chord. Path A: a dashed vertical from typed 0.5 marks the average of the typed numbers, a marker on the horizontal axis labelled '0.5'. Path B: a dashed horizontal at light 0.32 (the average of the two lights) runs to the curve and drops to the horizontal axis at '0.6'. Both markers stay on the axis, labelled 'average the typed numbers' and 'average the light'.
B30.motion_claim: Two dashed paths trace to two different markers on the axis, 0.5 and 0.6.

show.event: the curve with the two grays on it and their chord
path B: light average, marker 0.6; settled through 60 %

B30.why: Two paths to two numbers on one axis make 'same colors, two answers' visible; the renders in the previous beat show the pixels, this shows why.

props.title: The same blend, three renderers

B31.visual_intent: A three-row table, one row ringed as each renderer is named, the third column carrying the real measured pixel and the fourth saying where each renderer is the default (desktop, mobile devices, web), which defines Mobile where it is first spoken.
B31.motion_claim: The ring steps down the rows with the voice.
B31.why: Three parallel facts with a measured number each is what the table component is for; the previous beat already showed the picture.
